claims: Forecasters and climate agencies are predicting a potential super El Niño in late 2026 following a rapid transition from La Niña.
NOAA has issued an El Niño watch.
NOAA's El Niño watch indicates a 62% chance of El Niño development by June–August 2026.
An El Niño watch is in effect.
There are expectations of El Niño developing in early-to-mid summer 2026.
There are expectations of El Niño strengthening by fall/winter.
There is a roughly 1-in-3 chance of a strong or super El Niño event.
A super El Niño occurs when equatorial Pacific ocean temperatures reach 2°C or more above average.
El Niño typically brings wetter, cooler conditions to the Southern U.S.
El Niño typically brings warmer, drier conditions to the North U.S.
The potential 2026 super El Niño follows a period of extreme ocean heat.
Experts advise that climate models have higher uncertainty in spring.
Experts advise that climate models will become more accurate closer to summer.
